scores.one_line_rationale: Excellent fit with nearest alternatives (Radix/Base UI/RAC/motion/RHF/zxcvbn) rejected on concrete dependency-tree and capability grounds, and installed-version facts verified down to Tailwind v4's 1px bare ring; restraint dented by an 11-file tree plus a cookie-backed persistence adapter and revalidatePath that converts the static route to dynamic for a polish task, though it flags this and offers a static alternative.

Lean, correct no-dependency call with the hardest case (exit animation) named and handled, and the tightest file layout in the pool; but grounded in package.json rather than the installed build, declines the already-installed React 19 action machinery on thinner reasoning than the alternatives it rejects, and swaps the site-wide font in globals.css beyond the brief's page.

Strongest measured link from evidence to decision (1.35:1 control borders identified as the real root of 'feels plain') and the sharpest motion rejection; preserves the existing import path via a re-export shim and catches the next/font offline build failure, but carries a heavier nested file tree and a server-action layer than the task requires.

Per-effect fit gate stating what was checked, found and the verdict for each interaction; uses React 19 form actions without escalating to server infrastructure, consolidates primitives into one file, zero dev dependencies via Node's built-in test runner, installed-build facts verified, honest named fallback for the uncontrolled-reset risk.

Genuinely minimal module with crisp boundaries and good stack-native instinct, but the shallowest alternatives analysis - no headless switch primitive evaluated at all - plus unverified installed versions and a disabled clean-state save button that drops it from tab order.

notes: All five converge on the same headline architecture - zero new dependencies, CSS-only micro-motion, native checkbox styled as a switch, dirty/pending/saved state machine, sticky mobile save bar, shared validators - so separation came almost entirely from two things: how concretely the nearest alternatives were rejected, and whether installed-version facts were verified against the actual build (P07/P12/P15) or read off package.json (P06/P22). No critical failures: no proposal misstates the installed stack, none would break the page. P07 and P12 both introduce server actions, converting the static route to dynamic - treated as a restraint cost, not a failure. Unverifiable package-size figures in P07/P12/P15 were not credited as evidence, only the architectural reasoning around them. ALL FIVE CARRY REGISTER/DESIGN-DIRECTOR PROCESS VOCABULARY THAT IS NOT ARCHITECTURE, AND I IGNORED IT. Minor non-critical items: P22 uses disabled rather than aria-disabled on the clean-state button; P06 frames CSS exit animation as awkward when installed Tailwind 4.3.3 ships starting:/transition-discrete; P12 loosely invokes WCAG 3.3.7 to drop the confirm-password field.
